segments.text: Welcome to your daily Robotics news digest for September 18th, 2026.
Today we're diving into ROS updates, including native ROS 2 on Zephyr and a new PX4 demo in Gazebo.
From Planet ROS, ROS Discourse General: Native ROS 2 on Zephyr with Cyclone DDS.
This report details the implementation of native ROS 2 on the Zephyr operating system utilizing Cyclone DDS as the underlying middleware.

Testing demonstrated that the current software stack, which includes rclc, rcl, rmw_cyclonedds_c, and Cyclone DDS running on an ESP32-S3 via Wi-Fi, permits the board to join the DDS/RTPS network directly without requiring a Micro XRCE-DDS Agent.
Testing was conducted using the stock ROS 2 Lyrical stack, which supports fixed-size messages and best-effort Quality of Service settings.
Future development plans involve extending this architecture to incorporate features such as Reliable Quality of Service and DDS Security.
This advancement shows a pathway for deploying ROS 2 capabilities directly onto resource-constrained embedded systems.
From Planet ROS, "ROS Discourse General: New SMACC demo in Gazebo using the PX4 flight stack".
This report details a demonstration utilizing the new SMACC PX4 Client Library to autonomously control a drone within the Gazebo simulation environment.
The key result is the successful integration and demonstration of the SMACC and PX4 flight stack specifically within the simulated geography of the Strait of Hormuz.
The process involved connecting ROS2, PX4, SMACC2, and Gazebo simulation to achieve autonomous drone control.
The source code for this application is available on GitHub, and the process and usage instructions are documented in the application's readme file.
This work establishes a functional connection between these distinct systems for complex aerial navigation simulation.
This development signifies a tangible step forward in simulating real-world autonomous flight systems using integrated robotics frameworks.
Further advancements in simulation and control system integration are anticipated.
And that's all for today's robotics roundup!
Keep building those brilliant minds, and we'll see you tomorrow for more tech adventures.
